body.cap: LBS Tech introduces “MaaS-Bridge” at CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: LBS Tech Co., Ltd. (CEO Siwan Lee) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time).

LBS Tech began with pedestrian information services for the visually impaired and wheelchair users and has expanded its business into future mobility areas such as autonomous driving, delivery robots, and smart cities by advancing the technologies it has accumulated over the years for collecting, classifying, and processing pedestrian pathway data.

In particular, the company defines pedestrian pathways as a core data asset that conventional maps and navigation technologies cannot adequately address. It precisely collects factors that directly affect actual movement, including pathway width, slope, surface condition, level differences, and obstacles, and processes them according to disability types and user characteristics to provide optimal routes.

By presenting the potential of a “door-to-door” service that connects the moment a user exits a vehicle to the entrance of the destination, LBS Tech earned the honor of winning the Best of Innovation Award in the Travel & Tourism category at CES 2026.

At the CES 2026 venue, “MaaS-Bridge” appeared as the Best of Innovation Award–winning solution and a new mobility connection system designed for the autonomous driving era. While existing MaaS (Mobility as a Service) focuses on vehicle-centered, integrated mobility services, the company explained that its solution specializes in addressing the disconnect between vehicles and pedestrian pathways.

MaaS-Bridge comprehensively analyzes traffic flow on vehicle roads, the condition of nearby pedestrian pathways at destinations, and user mobility characteristics to design customized pick-up and drop-off points for different user types. By defining so-called “Mobility Points (MP),” the system guides users from vehicle drop-off locations to safe and highly accessible pedestrian pathways.

The core of these technologies lies in expanding the activity radius of mobility-vulnerable groups beyond urban movement into leisure and travel. This is significant because it broadens the scope of activities for people with visual impairments, wheelchair users, and older adults beyond city travel into wider domains.

LBS Tech has already demonstrated its technological competitiveness both domestically and internationally. In 2023, the company received an award at the Mobile World Congress in the Best Mobile Use Case category for accessibility and inclusivity, and at the previous CES, it earned an Innovation Award in the Human Security for All category. In Korea, it carried out pedestrian pathway data construction projects with the Korea Labor Force Development Institute for the Aged and the Korea Employment Agency for Persons with Disabilities, and implemented services utilizing pedestrian data in major smart city projects such as Sejong Smart City and Busan Eco Delta City.

The company also continues to expand overseas pilot cases. In 2024, it demonstrated an AR-based mobile pedestrian navigation service in Barking and Dagenham, London, followed in 2025 by a pilot AR pedestrian mobility and tourism information service for mobility-vulnerable users in Birmingham through collaboration with the West Midlands Combined Authority. It also plans to work with Aston University to develop an integrated pedestrian environment system linked with autonomous driving technologies.

Building on its participation at CES 2026, LBS Tech plans to expand its collaborations with global companies and accelerate its entry into North American and European markets. The company will conduct proofs of concept in regions with high awareness of autonomous driving technologies and universal mobility rights, verifying the importance of pedestrian technologies in the final stages of autonomous driving. In particular, it plans to develop technologies for automatically classifying accessibility suitability using AI-enabled cameras, aiming to overcome data-collection limitations for overseas service localization.

An LBS Tech official said, “CES 2026 provided an opportunity to directly validate on the global stage how important pedestrian technologies are within the autonomous driving ecosystem,” adding, “We will continue to build an inclusive mobility environment where everyone, including mobility-vulnerable groups, can move freely in travel and everyday life.”

The Incheon Metropolitan City Government and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority formed the “INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion” at LVCC North Hall during CES 2026, presenting Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as it evolves beyond a smart city into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs, including Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Awards Showcase, the pavilion supported the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES, including 10 companies exhibiting at the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion. In particular, 14 companies won 17 CES Innovation Awards, marking the largest achievement to date and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovative enterprises.
